title: You think you’re a good person.
paragraphs:
You think you’re a good person.
That’s exactly why this message will shake you.

Because if “being good” could get you into heaven…
then why did Jesus have to die?
Pause.
Let that question sit.

We built a quiet belief system in our hearts:
“I’m not perfect… but I’m not that bad.”
We compare.

At least I’m not like them.
At least I try.
At least I help people.
At least I go to church sometimes.
But Scripture doesn’t grade on a curve.
It reveals a mirror.

“None is righteous, no, not one.” (Romans 3:10)
“For all have sinned and fall short of the glory of God.” (Romans 3:23)

Not the addict.
Not the liar.
Not the one hiding secrets in the dark.
All.
Including the “good” ones.

Including the disciplined ones.
Including the generous ones.
Including the ones who look clean on the outside but are quietly breaking inside.
This is where the tension rises.
Because if God is truly holy—not just “better than us,” but completely pure—then even one sin is not small.
It’s cosmic rebellion.
And suddenly, “good enough” collapses.
Here’s the truth most people avoid:

You don’t need to be worse to need saving.
You already do.
Even your best day cannot erase your worst sin.
Even your kindness cannot cancel your guilt.
Even your morality cannot resurrect your dead spirit.
That’s not condemnation.
That’s clarity.

Because right here—right at the breaking point—
grace enters the story.

Not soft grace.
Not cheap grace.
Blood-bought grace.
Jesus Christ didn’t come for people who had it together.
He came for people who finally admit they don’t.
“God shows His love for us in that while we were still sinners, Christ died for us.” (Romans 5:8)

Not when you improved.
Not when you cleaned yourself up.
Not when you became “worthy.”
While you were still a sinner.
That’s the scandal.
That’s the beauty.
Picture this.
A courtroom.
You’re standing guilty.

No excuses left.
No arguments strong enough.
The verdict is just.
And then—
Someone steps forward.
Not to defend your innocence.
But to take your sentence.
Jesus doesn’t say, “They’re not that bad.”

He says,
“I will pay for everything.”
And on the cross, He did.
“He Himself bore our sins in His body on the tree…” (1 Peter 2:24)

Every hidden thought.
Every secret habit.
Every word you wish you could take back.
Paid.

Not ignored.
Not minimized.
Paid in full.
This is why the message matters:
Heaven is not for good people.
Because if it were, nobody would enter.
Heaven is for those who have been forgiven, washed, made new through Jesus Christ.
“For by grace you have been saved through faith… not a result of works.” (Ephesians 2:8–9)
You don’t earn it.
You receive it.
And here’s the moment that changes everything:
You can keep trying to prove you’re good enough…

Or you can finally admit you’re not—
and trust the One who is.
That’s called repentance.

Turning from self-reliance.
Turning from sin.
Turning toward Christ.
Not just knowing about Him.
Surrendering to Him.
Some scholars interpret repentance as merely a change of mind.
But Scripture shows it’s deeper.

It’s a change of direction.
A reorientation of the heart.
A laying down of pride.
And when that happens?
You are not just “improved.”
You are reborn.
“If anyone is in Christ, he is a new creation.” (2 Corinthians 5:17)
Not patched up.
Not slightly better.
New.
So here’s the real question:
Are you trusting your goodness?
Or are you trusting Jesus?
Because one will fail you the moment you stand before God.
And the other has already secured your place.
This isn’t about fear.
This is about truth.
And truth, when it cuts deep enough, can finally heal.
If something inside you is stirring right now…
That’s not accident.
That’s invitation.
You don’t need a perfect prayer.
You need a surrendered heart.
You can say:

“Lord Jesus, I know I’m not righteous.
I’ve sinned.
I can’t save myself.
But I believe You died for me and rose again.
Forgive me.
Make me new.
I surrender to You.”
And He will not turn you away.
“Whoever comes to Me I will never cast out.” (John 6:37)
This is eternity-level truth.
This is life and death.
This is grace standing at your door.

Good people don’t go to heaven.
Forgiven sinners do.
And that means there is hope.

For you.
Right now.
